messages.subject: Fisher Exact Test
parts:
I coded up the example given by Andrew Gelman

http://andrewgelman.com/2009/10/13/what_is_the_bay/

and Bob Carpenter

https://lingpipe-blog.com/2009/10/13/bayesian-counterpart-to-fisher-exact-test-on-contingency-tables/

in stan.

data {
  int n1;
  int n2;
  int y1;
  int y2;
}

parameters {
  real theta1;
  real theta2;
}

model {
  theta1 ~ beta(1.0, 1.0);
  theta2 ~ beta(1.0, 1.0);
  y1 ~ binomial(n1,theta1);
  y2 ~ binomial(n2, theta2);
}

generated quantities {
  real thetaDiff;
  thetaDiff = theta1 - theta2;
}

But I get many messages of the form

Exception thrown at line 14: beta_log: Random variable is -0.00885988, but must be >= 0! 

and

Exception thrown at line 15: beta_log: Random variable is 4.59635, but must be less than or equal to     1

I looked at

See http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#exception-hamiltonian-proposal-rejected

but wasn’t much the wiser.

I also stared at the `pairs` plot but was unable to deduce very much.

I go the expected answer but I am slightly concerned about all the warnings (I ran 4 chains with warmup of 1000 for 10,000 steps).

Dominic Steinitz
dom...@steinitz.org
http://idontgetoutmuch.wordpress.com

messages.subject: Re: Fisher Exact Test
parts:
On Tuesday, January 17, 2017 at 7:31:10 AM UTC-5, idontgetoutmuch wrote:
data {
  int n1;
  int n2;
  int y1;
  int y2;
}

parameters {
  real theta1;
  real theta2;
}

That should be

parameters {
  real<lower=0, upper=1> theta1;
  real<lower=0, upper=1> theta2;
}

Ben
